fonts._doc: Type roles, taken from the lyric-mv kit: mono = labels / numbers / code, serif = the voice that speaks, sans = the interface. Files live in vendor/fonts (SIL OFL 1.1, @fontsource), so the deck renders identically on every machine and needs no network. The deck uses them as: kicker + stat numbers + footnote = mono, headline + body = sans, quote = serif. `cjk` is appended to every role: the bundled faces are Latin-only, so without it a Chinese kicker falls back unpredictably and dense characters (翻, 暖) become black blobs at small sizes.

palettes._doc: DECK THEMES. One theme per page, chosen by what the page is for — colour is a STATE entered by an event in the song, never redecorated page by page. Roles: bg page, panel darker surface, raised cards/plates, line hairlines, text the headline, sub secondary text, mute tertiary, me / meHot / meDim the accent (its hot and dim ends), err the error red, bloom the tint the light takes. glow = bloom multiplier, sat = how much colour the art keeps. RAISED MUST SEPARATE FROM BG: measured on a real deck, a raised only ~10 ΔL from bg makes a cards/cycle page measure ~1% ink — the card is invisible and only its hairline border reads. Every raised here is >=19 ΔL from its bg.

glow._doc: Bloom strength = (...) * theme.glow, and only SATURATED pixels feed it: between satKnee[0] and satKnee[1] saturation a pixel goes from no bloom to full bloom, so paper-white UI stays matte while the accent glows. On a LIGHT theme (warm-paper / clean-white) lower this, or the page itself becomes the light source.

post._doc: Full-frame finish. grain and vignette are always on (they are what makes a flat render read as film); aberration and scanlines are small on purpose.
